stories.title: Association of sedentary behavior and physical performance with dysmobility syndrome among middle-aged and older adults: a PoCosteo study
stories.description: Aging independently increases the risk for chronic functional decline, even in the absence of illness. In this context, dysmobility syndrome (DS) has emerged as a major contributor to disability in middle-aged and older adults. This study aims to assess the prevalence of DS and its associated factors among middle-aged and older adults in Bushehr province, Iran. This cross-sectional analysis utilized data from the Iranian arm of the PoCOsteo project. DS, sedentary behavior, physical performance, and balance were assessed using standardized criteria and validated tests. Associations between DS and related variables were examined using multivariable logistic regression analyses. Among 1999 participants age 50 + mean 62.15 years, 1142 individuals (57.1%) were diagnosed with DS. Higher sedentary time during both workdays (OR: 1.81; 95% CI 1.16–2.81) and holidays (weekend) (OR: 1.64; 95% CI 1.08–2.50) was significantly associated with higher odds of DS. Conversely, better balance performance was associated with lower odds of DS (OR: 0.40; 95% CI 0.27–0.61). Each one-second increase in five-times sit-to-stand was associated with 6% higher odds of DS (OR: 1.06; 95% CI 1.03–1.08). Sedentary behavior and poorer physical performance were significantly associated with higher odds of DS among middle-aged and older adults.

stories.title: Towards molecular-based functional classification of fetal bovine serum
stories.description: Quality and price of fetal bovine serum (FBS) are traditionally determined by geographical origin and parameters listed in the Certificate of Analysis (CoA). Despite its central role in cell culture, selecting suitable FBS batches remains costly and labor-intensive due to substantial batch-to-batch variation. We propose a molecular assessment strategy based on transcriptomic and cytokine profiling of cells cultured in different FBS batches to evaluate performance more reliably. Analysis of differential gene expression in three cell lines—MRC-5, Jurkat, and THP-1—enables batch grouping and reveals pathway-specific effects, with immune-related pathways showing the most pronounced variability. Although CoA parameters can stratify batches by origin, they do not consistently correlate with cytokine secretion or gene expression across cell lines. These findings demonstrate that geographical origin is an inadequate predictor of functional FBS performance and that molecular profiling provides a more robust and informative assessment.

stories.title: A German online cross-sectional survey on herbal medicinal products for the treatment and management of gynaecological ailments
stories.description: Menstrual and menopausal ailments, as well as uncomplicated urinary tract infections, are the most common non-life-threatening gynaecological ailments. They are usually treated with standard chemically defined or/and herbal medicines. Although there have been surveys of affected women on perception, impairment and personal management of gynaecological ailments, the use of medication using real-world data based on everyday practice is poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, we aimed to obtain information on how affected women deal with their symptoms, with a particular focus on medication choice, patterns of use, and self-perceived effectiveness of the treatments applied. We developed a questionnaire and conducted an online survey with affected women. The results were analysed quantitatively using descriptive statistics and qualitatively by content analysis with subsequent inductive category formation. The present explorative analysis focuses on 268 women who reported about gynaecological symptoms. Our study population consisted predominantly of young (21–30 years, 74%) female students. As a result, we received limited information about menopausal symptoms and therefore excluded these cases from the quantitative analyses. The majority (~ 50%) of women stated that they did not perceive significant impairment in their everyday life due to their ailments, although most of them reported to have severe symptoms. Only 18% of the women took sick leaves. However, it remained unclear if they stayed away from work for 1 or 2 days, which is possible in Germany. Almost a quarter (18%) did not treat their (severe) symptoms because they perceived it as something they had to endure. The women who utilized drugs predominantly took non-herbal medicines. Those who treated their symptoms with herbal medicines perceived their effectiveness and tolerability as very good. Unexpectedly, a considerable share of women reported not treating their ailments, and those who did were more likely to prefer non-herbal medicines. The awareness about available treatment options appeared limited, even within this predominantly young and highly educated study population. These findings may indicate gaps in patient information and communication regarding therapeutic options that could be improved by fostering the dialogue between patients and healthcare professionals. Furthermore, it is important that future studies be conducted in larger and more representative populations to robustly confirm these observations, in particular regarding herbal medicine use in menstrual ailments and uUTIs; findings on menopausal symptoms remain preliminary and qualitative in nature due to the small subgroup size.

stories.title: Design and hardware performance of a LoRa-based vehicle tracking system with local data storage infrastructure
stories.description: This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of a LoRa-based vehicle tracking system, emphasizing its hardware architecture and field performance. The system uses custom-built end nodes based on Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 (V3) boards (an ESP32-S3 microcontroller with an integrated Semtech SX1262 transceiver) and u-blox NEO-6 M GPS modules, which transmit position data to a centrally located LoRa receiver node. Unlike typical cloud-integrated LoRaWAN deployments, the network operates in a standalone point-to-point topology with an on-premise database server, eliminating any dependence on external network infrastructure. We detail the integration of the LoRa radio, GPS receiver and antennas, including a compact in-vehicle enclosure and an elevated receiver antenna. Three transmission schemes were implemented to coordinate multiple vehicles: fixed-interval broadcasting, randomized-interval transmission, and a beacon-synchronized TDMA protocol for collision avoidance. Field tests were conducted on a suburban coastal highway and in a dense urban downtown area. Measurements are reported as path loss versus transmitter-receiver separation and are analyzed separately for line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) conditions. Log-distance models fitted to the field data, referenced to the measured path loss at 100 m so that the fitted exponents are independent of transmit power and antenna gain, give n = 4.63 for the open suburban coastal route and n = 3.43 for the obstructed urban routes. Consistent reception extended to approximately 3.2 km on the suburban route with intermittent reception to 4.5 km, and to 1.0–1.5 km on the urban routes. Packet delivery rate averaged 85–90% on the suburban route and 83.5 +/- 10.5% across six urban trials. A collision model calibrated against the five-node measurements extends the scalability assessment to 50 nodes, and shows that beacon-synchronized TDMA sustains full delivery for up to 97 nodes at a 10 s update interval on a single channel, whereas unsynchronized access falls below 60% delivery beyond 20 nodes. Because TDMA updates each vehicle only once per cycle, the multi-vehicle mode is characterized as near-real-time rather than real-time. Datasheet-derived energy consumption is 4.44 J per delivered message in the as-built configuration, roughly seventy times that of a duty-cycled low-power design, which qualifies the low-power claim for this class of tracker. The results demonstrate that a standalone LoRa platform with local data handling is a viable, low-cost alternative to cellular or LoRaWAN trackers for small fleets, while highlighting remaining limitations in urban RF performance, payload security, energy efficiency, sample size and radiated-power compliance.
